A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and support reliable comparison of their text, equations, tables and figures. All supplied pages were inspected, including v1's appended reproducibility checklist; v2 contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original layer-wise masking experiments, benchmark comparisons, layer-selection ablations and masking-ratio analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original cross-model masking experiments, annotated attention analysis, intermediate-layer output experiments and comparative benchmark results.

M1.justification: V1 contrasts attention against layer 28 and softly suppresses low-scoring visual-token features at review layer 29. V2 instead describes contrasting against the final layer, segmenting high-scoring image regions, combining them with the original image and performing a second inference pass. This substantially changes the inference procedure, although Hellinger-based layer selection remains.

E1.justification: The six original benchmarks—GQA, VQAv2, OKVQA, VizWiz, TextVQA and DocVQA—remain, while v2 Table 1 adds MMBench evaluation. The new annotated-region study uses existing TextVQA samples, making the documented dataset expansion limited.

E2.justification: V2 adds CD and OPERA to the retained DoLA and ViCrop comparisons. It removes v1's standalone MLLM comparison table, including BLIP-2, Flamingo, IDEFICS and InternVL variants. Figure 13 additionally compares inference time against SAM and CLIP, substantially revising comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Layer-wise masking expands from two LLaVA configurations to seven architectures, and enhancement comparisons add Qwen2.5VL. V2 also introduces a protocol using 1,000 randomly selected, manually annotated TextVQA samples and a separate intermediate-layer logit-output experiment on Qwen2.5VL. These are substantive additions to the evaluation design.

E4.justification: V2 adds full layer-wise attention visualization, quantitative target-versus-noise attention analysis and early-output tests, while extending Hellinger-distance analysis across architectures. V1's masking-ratio sensitivity study disappears. The pre-integrated-layer selection ablation remains, largely redisplayed from v1 Table 3 as v2 Figure 11.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies concrete repeated-run counts, seed values, confidence intervals or significance tests. V1's checklist makes general reporting assertions but provides no actual run or seed information. V2's sample averages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds MMBench, Qwen2.5VL and new analysis results. Existing entries also change: DoLA's LLaVA VQAv2 score is 70.1 in v1 Table 2 versus 76.11 in v2 Table 1; shallow-selection TextVQA changes from 57.00 to 58.00 in Table 3/Figure 11. Several layer-distribution plots also receive different dataset labels. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V1's formal quantile-thresholded feature-scaling definition in Equation 4 is removed. The Hellinger-distance definition, argmax selection rule and attention-difference formula remain essentially unchanged. Neither version develops substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central methodological contribution changes from review-layer feature masking to early-versus-final attention-based image refinement and re-input. V2 also explicitly limits the late-review finding to certain architectures and broadens the claimed applicability beyond the LLaVA-focused contribution in v1.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies review behavior as architecture-dependent and interprets intermediate-layer answers and attention-distance patterns as additional evidence of fusion completion. It explains re-input as reinforcing relevant regions while preserving global context. V1's speculation linking masking-induced latency to disrupted reasoning pathways is removed.

D1.justification: V1's explicit 7B backbone specifications, 576-token masking instructions, RTX A800/PyTorch 2.0/Ubuntu 20.04 setup and code-release promise are omitted. V2 documents manual region annotation and an RTX A6000 for its new timing experiment, but provides no equivalent general implementation-settings description.

R1.justification: The core related-work discussion remains. V2 adds references for CD, OPERA, additional architectures and cross-modal information flow, while dropping references associated with removed standalone baselines. It more explicitly positions the method within ViCrop's re-input paradigm, emphasizing adaptive layer selection.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The exploration section gains a new hierarchical organization, and experiments previously grouped in Section 5 are integrated into the method section. V2 also expands the author information, adds acknowledgements and removes the appended checklist.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns the visual presentation: masking plots are regrouped by model, the method diagram is replaced, the selection-ablation table becomes bar charts, and new attention, fusion-layer, early-output and timing figures are introduced. Figure 1 and the layer-distribution charts are also rearranged and restyled.

improvement.justification: Seven-model masking, annotated attention measurements and early-output tests strengthen support for the fusion findings and their architectural boundaries. However, v2 removes useful experimental settings and leaves its redesigned inference procedure underspecified, including a final-layer definition that conflicts with the retained k = 28 statement. These evidentiary gains and reproducibility losses prevent a reliable net assessment of overall quality.
